# Atlas v2 — the polities that carried the wrong Wikidata item

*Generated by `.claude/atlas-build/audit-polity-names.js --qid-table` from `polity-qids.json`, `polity-qids-wikidata.json` and `atlas/data/history.bin`; do not edit. Wikidata is CC0.*

Where this comes from. Cliopatria names a Wikidata item and an English Wikipedia article on every row; `build-history.js` takes, for each series, the pair of the rows covering the most years. On some series that pair is a different thing from the polity (Han dynasty → Chauhan, a medieval Indian clan; Numidia → Jugurtha, a man). Phase 4's name audit found 63 of the 165 entities with a QID whose Wikidata label differs from their name, 102 agreeing; most of the 63 differ only in wording (“Venice” / “Republic of Venice”) and their item is right. This file is about the ones whose item is another thing.

## Counts

| | entities |
|---|---|
| carry a QID (polities 157, peoples 8) | 165 |
| **corrected** (wrong item, the right one unambiguous) | 26 |
| **unresolved** (wrong item, no unambiguous replacement; allowed by the check with a reason) | 3 |
| right item, let through by the check with a reason | 3 |
| doubtful, kept | 8 |
| unchanged otherwise | 125 |

Besides the 26 series whose main pair was replaced, 3 secondary pairs (“Also in the source” on the place card) were replaced. The check's two rules are in the header of `audit-polity-names.js`.

## Re-running

`node .claude/atlas-build/audit-polity-names.js --check` (offline; CI) proves the rules and the fixes against the committed Wikidata cache and `history.bin`. `--fetch-qids` refreshes the cache (network). After editing `polity-qids.json`: `--fetch-qids` for a new item, then `node --max-old-space-size=12000 .claude/atlas-build/build-history.js --no-cache --install` (docs/atlas-v2-build.md step 3: fresh, because a cache replay is not byte-identical), then `build-polity-index.js --install`, `node .claude/migrate-places.js` (see `check-places.js` for place rows that now duplicate a polity), and this table (`--qid-table`).
